Rakuten France - Multimodal Product Classification (27 classes)

Reproducible end-to-end pipeline: download → EDA → preprocessing → modelling → validation. Full corpus (84,916 products), strict 2-way train/test split (80/20, stratified, seed 42). Primary metric: macro-F1 on the held-out test set.

1. Executive summary

0.855
best macro-F1 (CamemBERT + ConvNeXt fusion)

Key findings.
1. Text beats image, and fusing both wins. The multimodal late-fusion of CamemBERT (text) + ConvNeXt-tiny (image) reaches 0.8552 macro-F1, beating text-only (0.8308) and image-only (0.7015). McNemar confirms the gain is statistically significant (p≈2e-25).
2. A French-specialist transformer is the best single model. CamemBERT (0.8308) edges out multilingual mBERT/XLM-RoBERTa despite the ~20% non-French tail.
3. Classical TF-IDF is a strong, cheap baseline. LinearSVC reaches 0.7912 - within ~0.04 of a fine-tuned transformer at a fraction of the cost.
4. The score is capped by a handful of overlapping classes (see per-class F1 and the confusion table), not by overall data quality - sanity checks pass cleanly.

3. Research questions & answers

#QuestionAnswer (from test-set results)
Q1Is text or image the stronger signal, and does fusion beat the best single modality?Text > image; fusion wins (0.8552 vs 0.8308 text / 0.7015 image).
Q2Which classical text model fits sparse TF-IDF best?LinearSVC 0.7912 > LogReg 0.7828 > XGBoost 0.7582 > RandomForest 0.7399 > NaiveBayes 0.6822 > DecisionTree 0.5828.
Q3French specialist vs multilingual transformer?French CamemBERT 0.8308 > mBERT 0.8102 / XLM-RoBERTa 0.8067, despite the non-French tail.
Q4Best image backbone?ConvNeXt-tiny 0.7015 > ViT-small 0.6767 > EfficientNet-B3 0.624 > B0 0.6016 > ResNet50 0.5629.
Q5Does SMOTE beat class-weighting, and threshold tuning help?SMOTE ≈ neutral on SVD (0.7109 vs 0.7113); per-class threshold tuning helps (0.7868 vs 0.7858).

4b. Compute environment & runtime per model

Two environments were used: CPU = Intel i9-14900HX (12-core), for the classical TF-IDF models; GPU = NVIDIA RTX 4070 Laptop (8 GB), for the fine-tuned transformers, image backbones, the multimodal fusion and the XGBoost BayesSearch. Times are wall-clock; transformer/image times come from the timestamped training log, classical times were measured by a single timed fit+predict, and the BayesSearch time is the full search.

Totals (sequential): GPU work ≈ 9 h 54 m, CPU classical ≈ 35 m 38 s. The GPU XGBoost BayesSearch dominates GPU time (deep 800-tree configs); the classical TF-IDF models each finish in seconds to a couple of minutes, which is why they remain attractive baselines. DistilCamemBERT and KNN-Bayes ran under concurrent load without per-model timestamps, so their wall-clock is not cleanly comparable and is omitted here (their scores are unaffected).

5. Methodology & per-phase findings

Phase 0 - Download

Raw text tables (X_train, Y_train) and product images are fetched into data/ via src/data/make_dataset.py.

Phase A - EDA & statistical checks

Joined text + labels, profiled text length and language, quantified missingness, and characterised the 13.4:1 class imbalance. Missingness of the description field is class-dependent, so rows were kept (title alone carries signal) rather than dropped.

Phase B - Preprocessing

Title+description merged, lowercased, stripped of URLs/HTML/numbers/symbols (accents kept), tokenised, FR+EN+DE stopwords removed, French stemming applied; images border-cropped and resized to 224. Output checkpoint data/df_clean.csv (all 84,916 rows).

Phase C - Modelling

TF-IDF (1,2)-grams (20k, min_df=3, sublinear); dense SVD-300 + SMOTE for tree/tuned models; a dimension-reduction comparison and a t-SNE projection; then the full model zoo (classical, transformers, image backbones) and equal-weight late fusion.

Phase D - Validation & interpretation

Cross-validation, per-class and confusion analysis, SHAP + LIME interpretability, fairness by language, McNemar significance, ablations, imbalance-handling comparison, and sanity controls.

6.9 Sanity controls

checkmacro-F1 / valueverdict
Majority-class baseline0.008floor - real models must beat this
Shuffled-label control0.0272~0 expected = no leakage
Memorise tiny train subset0.766high = model has capacity to fit
Real models (best 0.85) vastly exceed the majority baseline (~0.008) and the shuffled-label control (~0.03), and the model can memorise a tiny subset - so the pipeline is learning real signal with no label leakage.

7. Positioning vs literature

Classical ceilingTF-IDF + LinearSVC ~0.75-0.79 macro-F1
Multimodal (reported)frozen ResNet18 autocrop fusion ~0.80
SOTA (reported)fine-tuned CamemBERT/FlauBERT ~0.88-0.90 (biggest lever)
Techniques implementedSMOTE, per-class threshold tuning, weighted late fusion, CamemBERT frozen embeddings

8. Limitations & next steps

  • Biggest lever: the few overlapping class pairs (section 6.3) cap macro-F1 - targeted features or a pairwise re-ranker would help most.
  • Fusion is simple: equal-weight late fusion; a learned/attention fusion or joint fine-tuning could add more.
  • Image models are single-crop fine-tuned for a few epochs - more epochs / TTA would raise the image floor.
  • Language gap: minority-language F1 trails French; targeted augmentation or per-language calibration could narrow it.

9. Reproducibility

Every number above is read from the pipeline’s own JSON outputs at build time. Re-run end to end:

python src/data/make_dataset.py        # Phase 0  download
python src/features/build_features.py  # Phase A+B  EDA + clean -> data/df_clean.csv
python src/models/benchmark_all_models.py   # Phase C  classical (CPU)
python gpu_phase.py                    # Phase C  transformers + images + fusion (GPU)
python src/models/validate_model.py    # Phase D  validation/interpretability
python src/models/compute_metrics.py   # accuracy + macro/weighted-F1 table
python src/make_report.py              # Phase E  this report

Split: stratified 80/20, seed 42, no validation set. Tuning uses CV inside train only.
